known_gaps: Annotation is 0 of 30. Every judgement field on the unannotated rows is null and must render as "not yet annotated" rather than be skipped, or this file reads as finished when it is a third done.
Measured 30 of 30; 0 row(s) carry a failed or absent capture, which is a result rather than a gap to be filled in later.

This batch is step 1 of the CAPTURE.md ordering — government screens only, all platform "web". None of the coverage targets for screen_type can be assessed until annotation exists, because screen_type is an annotated field.

pre_2010 is 0 and cannot be anything else from live capture. The five old screens the brief asks for need archived material and a different method; nothing here will surface that absence except this line.

not_a_product, government and pre_2010 are counted from targets.json as capture-time claims. They have not been confirmed against the rendered page, and a row no longer listed in targets.json contributes to none of them.
Colour share is bounding-box area, not painted pixels, so a large transparent wrapper counts for nothing and a large white one counts for a lot.
1 row(s) were served with a non-2xx status and kept because the page rendered anyway: sd-scr-011 (400). Each needs a person to confirm the capture is the page it claims to be.
notes.method: Chromium 1440x900 at dpr 2, domcontentloaded + 2.5s, then getComputedStyle over the first 4000 body elements. Screenshots at 360, 768, 1440 CSS px. Grid is reported only where the page declares display:grid; where it does not, detected is "container" and columns is null rather than inferred.
notes.annotation_policy: capture_screens.mjs never writes the annotation object. It preserves whatever is there and creates it as null. Any annotation in this file was written by a person.
